b.13e6e2f4d6:
<h>Hymnus</h>
<c>V</c>írginis Proles, Opiféxque Matris,
Virgo quem gessit, peperítque Virgo:
Vírginis festum cánimus trophǽum
Accipe votum.

<h>H</h>æc tua Virgo dúplici beáta
Sorte, dum gestit frágilem domáre
Córporis sexum, dómuit cruéntum
Corpóre sæclum.

<h>U</h>nde nec mortem, nec amíca mortis
Sæva pœnárum génera pavéscens,
Sánguine fuso méruit sacrátum
Scándere cælum.

<h>H</h>uius obténtu, Deus alme, nostris
Parce iam culpis, vítia remíttens,
Quo tibi puri resonémus almum
Péctoris hymnum.

<h>G</h>lória Patri genitǽque Proli,
Et tibi compar utriúsque semper
Spíritus alme, Deus unus, omni
Témpore sæcli.
Amen.
b.1d2384938a:
<h>Hymn</h>
<c>S</c>on of a virgin, maker of thy mother,
Thou, rod and blossom from a stem unstainèd,
While we a Virgin's triumphs are rehearsing,
Hear our petition!

<h>L</h>o, on thy handmaid fell a two-fold blessing,
Who, in her body vanquishing the weakness,
In that same body, grace from heaven obtaining,
Bore the world witness.

<h>D</h>eath, nor the rending pains of death appalled her;
Bondage and torment found her undefeated:
So by the shedding of her blood attained she
Heavenly guerdon.

<h>F</h>ountain of mercy, hear the prayers she offers;
Purge our offences, pardon our transgressions,
So that hereafter we to thee may render
Praise with thanksgiving.

<h>T</h>hou, the All-Father, thou, the One-Begotten,
Thou, Holy Spirit, Three in One co-equal,
Glory be henceforth thine through all the ages,
World without ending.
Amen.

<n>3</n> Et liberásti corpus meum a perditióne, a láqueo linguæ iníquæ et a lábiis operántium mendácium, et in conspéctu astántium factus es mihi adiútor.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
Ex libro S. Ambrósii Epíscopi de Virgínibus
<r>Liber 1, post initium</r>
<c>H</c>ódie natális est Vírginis, integritátem sequámur. Natális est Mártyris, hóstias immolémus. Natális est sanctæ Agnétis, miréntur viri, non despérent párvuli, stúpeant nuptæ, imiténtur innúptæ. Sed quid dignum ea loqui póssumus, cuius ne nomen quidem vácuum laudis est? Devótio supra ætátem, virtus supra natúram: ut mihi videátur non hóminis habuísse nomen, sed oráculum Mártyris, quod indicávit, quid esset futúra. Nomen Vírginis títulus est pudóris. Appellábo Mártyrem: prædicávi satis. Prolíxa laudátio est, quæ non quǽritur, sed tenétur. Nemo est laudabílior, quam qui ab ómnibus laudári potest. Quot hómines, tot præcónes, qui Mártyrem prǽdicant, dum loquúntur. Hæc trédecim annórum martýrium fecísse tráditur. Quo destabílior crudélitas quæ nec minúsculæ pepércit ætáti; immo magna vis fídei, quæ étiam ab illa testimónium invénit ætáte.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Omnípotens, adoránde, colénde, treménde, benedíco te,
* Quia per Fílium tuum unigénitum evási minas hóminum impiórum, et spurcítias diáboli impollúto calle transívi.
<r>℣.</r> Te confíteor lábiis te corde, te totis viscéribus concupísco.
<r>℟.</r> Quia per Fílium tuum unigénitum evási minas hóminum impiórum, et spurcítias diáboli impollúto calle transívi.

<c>T</c>oday is the birthday of a Virgin; let us imitate her virginal innocence. It is the birthday of a Martyr; let us also bring sacrifice. The name of our Virgin to a guarantee of her purity. If I call her Martyr, already I have praised enough.
